topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, relates the lecture to preceding practicals, and outlines the main learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor virology, proto-oncogene discovery, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the investigation of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays to assess cell transformation.

topics.label: Classifications and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major classes of cancer-associated genes and examine how specific mutations disrupt normal regulatory mechanisms such as the cell cycle.

topics.label: Pathways and mechanisms of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinctions between sequence and chromosomal instability and detail the specific DNA repair, replication, and mitotic defects that generate them.

topics.label: Multi-step progression and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how the stepwise accumulation of mutations and inherited germline defects accelerate tumor development and influence clinical progression.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, suggests supplementary reading material, and previews the topic of the upcoming lecture.
